What are the three parts of the soul according to Plato, and how did he define the 'rational' part?

Item 1: According to Plato, the soul has three parts or components which he calls reason, spirit, and appetite. Item 2: The rational (or thinking) part is the highest in order. When a person moves from believing to thinking, he moves from the visible world to the intelligible world, from the realm of opinion to the realm of knowledge. Thinking is particularly the characteristic of the scientist.
